That is the one command whose value is destroyed by waiting, and it is new. Everything else in the workshop reads a record that will still be there tomorrow. A poll records an ABSENCE, and absence leaves no trace once it heals — the moment a late push ingests, the page looks exactly as though it had always been there. (3) WHAT e000028 ACTUALLY FOUND, and it is not about varve. Every completeness check in this workshop asks a binary — present or absent — against a source that back-fills, so "absent" is never a fact about the record; it is a fact about the record AND the clock you read it at. The right frame is RIGHT-CENSORED SURVIVAL DATA. A push not yet ingested is censored: not a success, not a failure, not discardable. Two things follow. The observed lag distribution is biased SHORT by construction (a lag is measurable only if the push arrived, and the ones still in flight are exactly the slow ones), so "five of five arrived" is worth less than it reads. And the permanent-loss rate is NOT IDENTIFIABLE at any finite observation: dropped mass sits at t=infinity and no amount of polling separates it from mass that has merely not come yet. That is e000025's boundary — alone you catch contradiction, never omission — restated so it says exactly how much is lost: not the lag, only the tail. The missing piece was never a second party. It is a WATCH: a client that writes down its polls is its own second party across time.
